contributions.who: The Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Education (Paul Waugh)
contributions.text: The Government have today published the early years foundation stage profile assessment data for the 2025/26 academic year. The Government have set a national ambition for 75% of children in England to achieve a good level of development by 2028, as set out in the “Giving every child the best start in life” strategy. Achieving this ambition requires a collective effort across schools, early years providers, local authorities, health services and wider family support services, including Best Start family hubs, recognising that children’s outcomes at the end of reception are shaped by their learning and development throughout the early years. Early childhood development is strongly associated with later outcomes, providing the foundation for achievements throughout school and beyond. Children who achieve a good level of development at age five are more likely to succeed at school and less likely to be not in education, employment or training later in life. The latest data shows strong progress towards this ambition, with 72.3% of children reaching a good level of development, an increase of 4 percentage points on last year.
